root_cause_audit.text:
# Root-cause and experiment-value audit

21 October 2026. This review supersedes the immediate two-run spending recommendation in
`../Next_Research_Direction_20261021.md`. That file remains a record of a proposed intervention, not a selected method.
No new long training, cluster connection, model inference or repository modification was performed for this review.
All new numerical analyses use existing local measurements.

## Direct answer

Representation learning is not an established root cause, nor has it been established as more likely than
architecture-induced feature dependence, source coverage, learned decision bias or annotation/subtype differences.
The previous recommendation selected an intervention before establishing a sufficient connection between its
assumptions and the measured failures. Its augmentation-only versus augmentation-plus-feature-loss comparison
could measure that recipe's benefit, but would not by itself identify the project's underlying blocker.

The best-supported problem description is class-dependent and direction-dependent transfer failure under
changes in acquisition cues, class/subtype composition and source support. This is a problem description with
measured components, not a claim to have uniquely identified a cause. Source coverage and class-conditioned
acquisition-cue transfer deserve the first problem-fit review. A global capacity deficit has less direct support.

Architecture, sampling and losses are intervention variables; learned representation is an intermediate outcome.
They are not mutually exclusive explanations that confusion matrices can uniquely separate.

## What the expensive architecture comparison did and did not buy

- The new reference establishes a same-code/data-seed control. The context variant is a controlled screening
  comparison of one extra encoder block, not a test of the whole MinkUNet family or NAS.
- Context improves source all-seven mIoU 84.34→84.66 while target falls 59.84→57.49. Target building and vehicle
  IoU fall 14.60 and 15.75 percentage points. This supports rejecting the particular candidate for the stated objective.
- The expected utility benefit is endpoint-sensitive: the source-selected-best comparison helps utilities, while
  final-to-final utility mean is lower for context. It is not a consistent architecture benefit across endpoints.
- The comparison adds capacity and computation at one location. The diagnosis never localized an error to
  encoder block3. It cannot distinguish insufficient capacity, wrong receptive support, source-specific cues,
  subtype coverage, or optimization as the main cause. One seed cannot reject all related depth variants.
- It was useful as candidate screening; it had low diagnostic value for the broader causal question. Presenting
  it as a way to substantially identify the blocker overstated its information value.

The classifier evaluation is a separate 28m45s inference job, not another full training. It correctly rejects the
saved replacement classifier. However, source mIoU falls 84.34→38.46 for reference-best, so this is not a
source-competent alternative whose target failure can discriminate decision learning from representation.
The source-competence requirement should have been central before describing the test as such a discriminator.
Numerically correct projection is necessary but does not make a fitted classifier scientifically informative.

## Existing evidence gives more specific distinctions

### Recognition errors within a class change across domains

Recall percentages below are recomputed from the already-saved full matrices. They do not depend arithmetically
on the relative frequency of other ground-truth classes, unlike precision and IoU.

| Fixed checkpoint / class | Own-domain test recall | Other-domain test recall |
|---|---:|---:|
| ECLAIR M0 / vehicles | 87.29 | 15.11 |
| ECLAIR M0 / poles | 89.03 | 29.97 |
| DALES M0 / buildings | 95.35 | 78.43 |
| DALES Mix3D / buildings | 96.25 | 58.40 |
| DALES OCons / buildings | 95.33 | 48.33 |
| DALES BEV / buildings | 94.79 | 46.61 |

The problem cannot be summarized as changed class frequencies affecting metric arithmetic alone. It includes
changes in prediction behavior conditional on a common label. These may still arise from scene context,
different subtypes, annotation, acquisition, inputs, or feature/decision learning; this is not proof of one of them.

For an additional descriptive check, row-normalize each confusion matrix and apply identical class priors to
source and target. Under uniform common-class priors, the new reference gives hypothetical 82.13% versus
60.93% mIoU; conditional failures remain. Other reference priors yield different aggregate gaps and can even
reverse their signs. Thus no causal percentage of the gap should be attributed to composition from this calculation.
It does not change predictions or canonical scores. It also does not rule out a classifier's learned training-prior
bias or changes in the context seen by each point. Pure label shift assumes unchanged class-conditional inputs;
that is a strong model assumption, not established for these datasets (Lipton et al., ICML 2018).

### Acquisition-cue changes are class-specific

Aggregating the existing complete raw-point scan records gives the following fraction of points whose pulse
has `number_of_returns = 1`. This uses the same five-bin encoding as the current feature pipeline.

| Common class | DALES training (26 source-training tiles) | ECLAIR test (125 tiles) |
|---|---:|---:|
| Buildings | 83.32% | 83.23% |
| Poles including target towers | 3.82% | 42.45% |
| Vehicles | 71.71% | 91.00% |
| Vegetation | 14.37% | 20.20% |

These are class-conditioned raw-point marginal distributions, not post-voxel features, independent objects,
joint return-pair distributions, or causal sensitivity estimates. Class/subtype mixture and acquisition change
together. The pole shift is real in these files, but not proven to be sensor-only or responsible for the errors.
Near-identical building number-of-returns marginals do not prove all building input cues are stable: return number,
joint attributes, voxel pooling, spatial arrangement, scene context and annotation may differ.

This provides a concrete reason to investigate class-conditioned cue compatibility, while also arguing against
deleting returns or assuming one global return/density change explains every class.

### Support, subtype mixture and decisions already have measured signatures

- ECLAIR M0 replay contains vehicles in 21/72 selected items versus 71/72 in DALES M0, with accepted common
  vehicle fractions 0.0774% versus 1.2363%. This establishes an exposure difference, not its causal share of error.
- Target common-pole labels combine 7,010 ordinary-pole and 9,828 tower points. The new reference recalls
  about 72.77% of ordinary poles but 28.74% of towers. This establishes heterogeneous failure, not absence
  of tower-like examples in DALES. Source subtype coverage is not currently demonstrated.
- Wire→pole predictions contribute heavily to pole false positives. Raising pole weighting can increase recall
  while worsening precision, so a generic rare-class intervention is not a sufficient targeted explanation.
- Suppressing non-common ECLAIR outputs changes fixed-weight DALES vehicle predictions. The diagnostic
  vehicle IoU moves 14.93→18.42 for M0, with large errors remaining. Output competition contributes to that
  decision rule, but removing outputs is not a replacement canonical evaluation or proof of a trained remedy.

## Hypothesis status

| Explanation | Current evidence strength | What has not been established |
|---|---|---|
| Evaluation arithmetic / methods inactive as main cause | Strongly deprioritized by reproduction and execution checks | Every historical training trajectory is reproduced |
| Input mixed-label cells are the sole utility bottleneck | Strongly deprioritized by label-survival diagnostic | Raw geometric information and later processing are adequate |
| Evaluation class proportions alone | Insufficient as a complete empirical account; within-class rates differ | Learned prior bias is irrelevant |
| Source exposure and subtype support mismatch | Exposure and target subtype mixture are directly measured; missing source subtype support remains a hypothesis | Sampling alone solves the utility/generalization objective |
| Class-conditioned acquisition-cue/shape/context shift | Actual marginal cue differences and conditional prediction differences are measured | Which changed cue causes which error; acquisition versus morphology versus annotation |
| Poorly learned transfer representation | Plausible; not specifically identified | Feature alignment, DCGL or a point branch will fix it |
| Wrong architecture / insufficient global capacity | Open; weaker direct causal support | The backbone is either optimal or incapable; a failure at one layer was localized |
| Focal/Lovasz/normalization as dominant cause | Open, with historical-loss provenance limitations | A modern loss or normalization is the correct next spending choice |

## What the suggested methods actually change

DGLSS is a method in Kim et al., CVPR 2023. It constructs sampled views and adds sparsity-invariant feature
consistency plus semantic-correlation consistency. The latter constrains relations between class prototypes
(class-level feature summaries). It changes the learning objective and internal features, not simply class frequency
through over/undersampling. It still depends on the sampled views being relevant (Kim et al., CVPR 2023).

DCGL is the framework in He et al., ICCV 2025. It builds category-level feature embeddings, uses an auxiliary
semantic learning objective on those embeddings, and aligns embeddings from original and simulated clouds.
It also changes training objectives. Its geometric embedding is a learned feature-space construction, not a
guarantee of using only physical XYZ shape. It includes intensity and adverse-weather simulation in its original
form, so it is not a drop-in ALS experiment (He et al., ICCV 2025).

The earlier proposal's A arm was indeed another sampling-augmentation intervention. B added a representation
objective, not a class-frequency sampler. This distinction is technically real but does not establish priority.
An A/B comparison can isolate that added component's observed benefit in the chosen recipe; it cannot by
itself diagnose the whole transfer mechanism. In particular, forcing consistency between an original cloud and
an arbitrary thinned cloud does not establish that the real cross-dataset cue differences have been addressed.

## Correct next decision

Withdraw the immediate DGLSS/DCGL-derived two-training-run recommendation as not yet justified by problem fit.
Do not replace it with another architecture or loss proposal by elimination.

The prioritized research question is: for the failed classes, does training lack the relevant asset/subtype examples,
or does it learn decisions tied to acquisition-specific cues that change for otherwise comparable assets? Keep
annotation compatibility as a competing explanation. Those questions distinguish coverage-aware learning,
cue robustness and architecture inductive bias more directly than a generic extra-block test.

For a method to become the next training candidate, require:
1. A specific measured failure signature it addresses, beyond low target IoU or the word 'geometry'.
2. A valid input/label/observation contract for these ALS data. No absent intensity or unverified vehicle-beam geometry.
3. A concrete mechanism connecting the signature to the change, and a counter-explanation it can distinguish.
4. A prespecified measurable contrast, source-competence guard and interpretation of positive AND negative outcomes.
5. Realistic runtime/storage and all-class guardrails; no full sweep disguised as one submission.

The already-collected scans support paper problem-fit review now. The specific evidence still missing for a stronger
causal decision is representative error-linked cue/geometry/subtype support: whether incorrect points differ in
those cues from correctly predicted comparable examples, and whether source examples cover the failed target
subtypes. Dataset-wide marginal histograms and the tiny capped target-pole feature cohort cannot settle that.
This is a precise gap, not a request for another generic diagnostic campaign. No new collection or long run is
authorized or required merely to read this review; its expected discriminatory value must be specified first.

## Files and validation

- `class_composition_analysis.json`: all eight historical canonical source/target model pairs plus the current
  reference/context best models, recalculated from full matrices. Pure-composition and changed-recognition
  synthetic sanity checks pass. Canonical mIoUs match the recorded integer confusion matrices.
- `existing_return_histogram_analysis.json`: all 1,286 existing scan records aggregated, with nonnegative count,
  shape and between-feature class-support consistency checks. No raw point cloud was reread.
- Scientific records: earlier diagnosis/repaired exposure reports, completed architecture findings and completed
  readout findings. These analyses do not alter the canonical benchmark or provide a new achieved score.

## References

Lipton, Z. C., Wang, Y.-X., & Smola, A. J. (2018). Detecting and correcting for label shift with black box predictors.
*Proceedings of the 35th International Conference on Machine Learning*, PMLR 80, 3122–3130.
https://proceedings.mlr.press/v80/lipton18a/lipton18a.pdf

Kim, H., Kang, Y., Oh, C., & Yoon, K.-J. (2023). Single domain generalization for LiDAR semantic segmentation.
*Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition*, 17587–17598.
https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2023/html/Kim_Single_Domain_Generalization_for_LiDAR_Semantic_Segmentation_CVPR_2023_paper.html

He, P., Li, L., Jiao, L., Shang, R., Liu, F., Wang, S., Liu, X., & Ma, W. (2025). Domain-aware category-level geometry
learning segmentation for 3D point clouds. *Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer
Vision*, 28324–28333. https://arxiv.org/pdf/2508.11265 (published ICCV paper).

readout_findings.text:
# Completed classifier control: job 44229

## Outcome

The job completed on cn02 in 28m45s (Slurm exit 0:0 and evaluation status complete). All three unique models
were evaluated on 11 DALES and 125 ECLAIR test tiles each. No new training or head fitting occurred.

The saved replacement classifier fails for both source and target. Keep the original reference classifier.

## Full-test summaries

Percentages; changes are percentage points. Source-best is primary; final is secondary.

| Model endpoint | DALES original → readout | Change | ECLAIR original → readout | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| reference best (epoch 162) | 84.34 → 38.46 | -45.88 | 59.84 → 17.47 | -42.37 |
| context best/last (epoch 200) | 84.66 → 42.83 | -41.83 | 57.49 → 25.67 | -31.83 |
| reference last (epoch 200) | 84.83 → 28.58 | -56.25 | 58.62 → 16.29 | -42.34 |

## Primary target per-class comparison

| ECLAIR test class | Reference original → readout | Change | Context original → readout | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| ground | 95.87 → 42.59 | -53.28 | 95.01 → 45.96 | -49.06 |
| vegetation | 95.89 → 68.39 | -27.49 | 94.99 → 91.93 | -3.06 |
| buildings | 37.75 → 0.46 | -37.29 | 23.15 → 0.31 | -22.84 |
| wires | 76.38 → 10.06 | -66.32 | 84.10 → 35.60 | -48.50 |
| poles | 10.80 → 0.11 | -10.69 | 13.42 → 5.18 | -8.24 |
| fence | 55.85 → 0.26 | -55.58 | 61.20 → 0.45 | -60.76 |
| vehicle | 46.33 → 0.41 | -45.93 | 30.59 → 0.24 | -30.35 |

## What this establishes

- All seven class IoUs decline on source and target for every endpoint. All balanced-screen conditions fail.
- The alternative readout is not a practical repair. Its pole recall can increase while precision and IoU collapse:
  reference-best target pole recall rises 47.07% → 63.09%, but precision falls 12.30% → 0.107%.
- Recomputed scores match matrices; original results exactly match the earlier fetched study evidence. Protocol,
  tile and class/subtype support match between classifiers. GPU projection smoke has zero feature/logit error;
  backbone parameters and normalization buffers were unchanged. No target labels fitted or selected the classifier.

## Limits and the next decision

- The readout was fitted on only 8,668 feature/label observations from class-centred, capped source patches, with
  additional inverse-frequency weighting; these are not necessarily 8,668 distinct raw points. Its selection used
  similarly bounded source validation. Full-tile inference supplies a different class mix and neighbourhood context.
- Limited feature coverage, class weighting and patch/full-tile differences are plausible contributors to this
  readout's failure. This experiment does not separate them or prove one is the cause.
- The classifier already fails badly on DALES: reference source mIoU falls 84.34% → 38.46%. Therefore it is not
  a source-competent alternative whose target failure could specifically diagnose cross-domain representation.
- Do not claim that focal/Lovasz is vindicated, that all classifier fixes fail, or that the backbone must be replaced.
- Correct the earlier conditional plan: a failed readout alone does not justify choosing a new representation for
  the next expensive run. Close this particular readout candidate; keep the reference. Further loss, depth or
  backbone training is not automatically justified by these results, and no new job has been submitted.

## Evidence

- completed_remote_evidence.json: one manual read-only SSH fetch, then the connection closed; monitor not restarted.
- verified_readout_analysis.json: independent aggregate/per-class recomputation and paired-input checks.
